findings.summary: On the 200 held-out Mirefield levels, Skua did not significantly differ from Plover-PG in mean normalized return (primary endpoint): paired t-test t=1.18, p=0.27, 95% CI [-0.84, 2.66] for the mean paired difference (Skua − Plover-PG).
findings.scope: 200 held-out Mirefield levels, normalized return (0–100), 10 seeds, paired t-test α=0.05
findings.caveats: Non-significant difference is not evidence of equivalence; CI includes both negative and positive values.

findings.summary: Skua achieved a significantly higher held-out success rate than Plover-PG (secondary endpoint): mean 44.63% vs 40.50%, paired t-test t=4.05, p=0.0029, 95% CI [1.82, 6.44] percentage points for the mean paired difference.
findings.scope: 200 held-out Mirefield levels, success rate (%), 10 seeds, paired t-test α=0.05
findings.caveats: Secondary endpoint; effect size is about 4 percentage points.

findings.summary: The improvement in success rate was not accompanied by a significant improvement in normalized return, indicating a mixed result across the two pre-registered metrics.
findings.scope: Both pre-registered endpoints on 200 held-out Mirefield levels
findings.caveats: No direct test comparing the two metrics; interpretation is based on the separate significance outcomes.

sentences.text: On the 200 held-out Mirefield levels, Skua did not significantly differ from Plover-PG in mean normalized return (primary endpoint; 62.95 ± 5.04 vs 62.04 ± 4.29; paired t-test t=1.18, p=0.27, 95% CI [-0.84, 2.66]).
However, Skua achieved a significantly higher held-out success rate (secondary endpoint; 44.63% ± 3.85 vs 40.50% ± 4.78; paired t-test t=4.05, p=0.0029, 95% CI [1.82, 6.44] percentage points).
Thus, the results are mixed: Skua improved the secondary success-rate metric but not the primary normalized-return metric relative to Plover-PG.
